case.case_title: Nalika Kumudini, Attorney-at-Law, (on behalf of Malsha Kumari) v. Nihal Mahinda, O.I.C. Hungama Police and Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, S.C. Application (F.R.) No. 615/95, decided on 28 August 1997

clause.text: Any person detained shall be brought before a judge and cannot be held without legal order.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner was unlawfully detained without being produced before a Magistrate, violating Article 13(2) of the Constitution.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed she was detained by police without being produced before a Magistrate and was subjected to torture during detention.
case_context.respondent_argument: The 1st respondent denied unlawful detention and claimed the injuries were caused by the petitioner’s father, denying police custody or detention.
key_facts: Petitioner was detained by police after arrest without production before a Magistrate.
She was tied and hung from a tree and assaulted while in police custody.
Medical evidence showed injuries consistent with unlawful detention and torture.
Petitioner was released only after intervention by an Attorney-at-Law.
No legal order was produced authorizing her detention.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: Article 13(2) requires that any detained person be brought before a judge and not held without legal authority. The Court found the petitioner was detained unlawfully without being produced before a Magistrate, violating this constitutional protection.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The Court relied on medical evidence and the petitioner’s credible affidavits to conclude she was unlawfully detained and tortured, and that the 1st respondent condoned and acquiesced in this unlawful detention.
principles_established: Detention without production before a judge is unlawful.
Police officers are responsible for ensuring detainees are produced before a Magistrate.
Unlawful detention and torture violate Article 13(2).
precedents_cited: Premadasa v. Officer-in-Charge of the Hakmana Police, S.C. 127/94

outcome.holding: The Court held that the petitioner was unlawfully detained without production before a Magistrate, infringing Article 13(2) of the Constitution.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: The Court awarded compensation and ordered protection against harassment by police.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(2) was central to the Court’s finding that the petitioner’s detention was unlawful and that her fundamental rights were violated, justifying the relief granted.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The Court held that the arrest and detention of the girl without producing her before a Magistrate were unlawful and that she was subjected to torture, infringing her rights under Articles 11, 13(1) and 13(2).
